text:
sara: FYI - customer (Jane @ Acme) reports a production failover from ap-southeast -> eu-west around 10:23 UTC, app latency spiked and they saw intermittent 401s. They say the app was healthy in AP. :confused:

Tom-support: Can you paste the request IDs or any headers they saw?

customer-jane: here are a couple request ids: req_8a3f and req_8a41. We also saw X-Region: eu-west on responses even though our tenant is pinned to ap-southeast. Latency went from 80ms -> 650ms.

mike-oncall: @sara grabbing logs now. Initial thought: probe heartbeat suppression might have caused the control plane to think AP pool was unhealthy and routed to EU.

jen-infra: pulling probe logs for ap-southeast. I see repeated probe skips from the healthcache service starting at 10:22:50 UTC: 

```
healthcache: skipping probe check for pool ap-southeast - last_successful=2025-09-10T10:19:00Z cache_ttl=600s
probe: heartbeat_sent region=ap-southeast id=probe-042
router: route decision tenant=acme -> fallback eu-west (policy=latency_safe)
```

Tom-support: cache_ttl=600s? That seems long if a transient auth issue hit. Could cause sticky fallback.

charlie-ml: Also seeing auth token rotation events around 10:21:30 (short-lived 401 bursts). Might be unrelated but could explain initial failures that triggered healthchecks.

mike-oncall: Repro attempt: I ran our synthetic probe from ap-southeast lambda to the tenant endpoint, with X-Region header forced to ap-southeast:

```
curl -v -H "X-Region: ap-southeast" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood-prod/acme/v1/health
```

Response I got had X-Region: eu-west and a 200, which matches customer seeing wrong-region routing.

jen-infra: Tracing into the routing cache: the cache key includes region + pool_hash. I found a race where a failed probe write could set an override flag for the tenant for the cache_ttl window. The override key was created by a failed auth callback that didn't clear on success.

Tom-support: Do we have repro steps to trigger the override in staging? I want to give the customer a way to validate while we patch.

jen-infra: Yes. Steps to reproduce locally (staging):
1) Start a lease in ap-southeast pool
2) Simulate auth rotation by returning 401 for the first probe attempt
3) Ensure next probe returns 200 but with a delayed cache-clearing ack
4) Observe routing override remains for cache_ttl (600s) and traffic routes to fallback region

Command snippets:
```
# simulate 401 on first probe
echo "401" > /tmp/probe_response_first
# then flip to 200 before cache TTL expires
```

customer-jane: We can run a test window but need a short workaround so customers don't hit high latency.

mike-oncall: Short-term mitigation: reduce healthcache override_ttl for affected tenants to 30s and force a cache flush for acme. Doing that now.

deploy-bot: roll/healthcache/override_ttl set acme=30s by mike-oncall - CANARY 1% -> 2% -> 10%

jen-infra: I flushed the cache for tenant acme (prefix: tenant:acme:health_override). Confirmed entries removed.

mike-oncall: Customer confirmation?

customer-jane: After cache flush and TTL change latency dropped back to 90ms and no more 401s. Thanks.

charlie-ml: Root cause summary: transient auth rotation caused a probe failure that left an override flag in healthcache for full TTL (600s). The override forced fallback routing to eu-west. Two fixes: 1) make probe failure writes idempotent and ensure clear-on-success path, 2) reduce default override_ttl from 600s -> 60s.

jen-infra: I'll open a deployment PR for the clear-on-success fix + unit test to cover the race, and a config change to 60s for override_ttl.

mike-oncall: PR link: https://git.redwood/infr/healthcache/pull/452 (canary planned). Rolling to ap-southeast first.

Tom-support: I'll reply to the customer with the mitigation steps and planned permanent fix ETA.

customer-jane: Appreciate the quick action. Please let me know when the permanent fix is deployed.

mike-oncall: marking incident resolved for now, monitoring ap-southeast for 24h. If anyone sees reoccurrence ping #incidents. :white_check_mark:
